title: Grateful Dead Live at Cincinnati Gardens on 1973-12-04
lineage: master soundboard cassette > reel > pcm > dat > cdr

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a brief but high‑energy 1973 Garden show, highlighted by a ripping Bertha and Mexicali Blues despite an abbreviated second set.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard source that listeners describe as clear and of good quality, though only a fragment of the concert is available.  Fans praise the tight first‑set work—especially the explosive Bertha, jaw‑dropping Mexicali Blues and soaring Eyes of the World—while lamenting the late start and truncated second set.  Overall sentiment is mixed because the performance shines musically but the set feels incomplete.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical moments (show quality ~3.5) and note a good soundboard recording (~4).  Weighted average yields a solid mid‑high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners report the tape is in great vault quality with clear mix; complaints focus on missing portions of the show rather than audio flaws.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert opened late and ran short, with an abbreviated second set.  Despite the truncated format, the first set delivered strong momentum and tight jams, while the remaining second‑set cuts still showcase classic Dead improvisation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Solo on Bertha described as 'incredible'; teasing Nobody's Fault But Mine; leaves it all on stage during jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass work noted as worth checking during Eyes of the World, adding to the groove.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby (Weir) mentioned for missing chord changes on Promised Land and earning his bell‑bottoms on the reprise; also referenced for talking about promoter issues.
